items.prose: A share price rises 40%, then falls 30%.
items.question: What is the net change, as a percentage? Use a minus sign for a fall.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the two growth factors.

byKey.added: You added the two moves. The fall acts on the higher price, so multiply the factors.
byKey.cross: You kept only the cross term, 40% × 30%. Add the two moves to it: 40 − 30 − 12.
byKey.sign: The price ends below where it started, so the change is a fall: −2%.

explain.text: The factors multiply: 1.4 × 0.7 = 0.98. So the price ends 2% lower, a net change of −2%. Adding the moves gives +10% and forgets that the fall acts on a higher price.

items.question: What is $\sqrt{7{,}300}$ to the nearest whole number?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the squares either side, then take one Newton step.

byKey.rounded-up: The root is about 85.44, which rounds down. 86² = 7,396 is too big.
byKey.decimal: You found the root of 730. Pair the digits from the decimal point: 73 00.

explain.text: 85² = 7,225 and 86² = 7,396, so the root lies between them. One Newton step gives 85 + 75/170 ≈ 85.44. To the nearest whole number that is 85.

items.prose: You invest £8,000 at 5% a year, compounded once a year.
items.question: What is it worth after three years, to the nearest pound?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply by 1.05 once for each year.

byKey.simple: You added 5% of £8,000 three times. Each year's interest earns interest too.
byKey.interest-only: That is the interest alone. Add the £8,000 you started with.

explain.text: Each year multiplies by 1.05: 8,000, then 8,400, 8,820 and 9,261. Each year's 5% includes last year's interest. Simple interest would give only £9,200.

items.prose: A test gives six options a question. A right answer scores +1, a wrong one −1/5, and a blank 0.
items.question: What does a blind guess earn on average, and should you guess once you can rule out two options?

options.text: 0 blind; +1/10 with two ruled out, so guess.

options.why: You took off the whole penalty. It applies only to the 5/6 of guesses that are wrong.
You left out the penalty on the 5/6 of guesses that are wrong.

options.text: 0 blind and 0 with two ruled out, so leave it blank.
options.why: You kept the blind value after ruling two out. With four left the right chance is 1/4: 1/4 − 3/4 × 1/5 = 1/10.

feedback.correct: Correct. Guess once any option is out.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Weigh the right chance against the wrong chance times the penalty.

explain.text: Blind: 1/6 × 1 − 5/6 × 1/5 = 0, so a blind guess is worth a blank. With two ruled out: 1/4 − 3/4 × 1/5 = 1/10. Any option you can rule out turns a guess into a gain.

items.question: Which order runs from least to most likely?

options.why: 3/8 is 37.5%, just below 38%. You rounded it up.
You ranked the fractions by the bottom number, largest first, and put 38% last. Turn each into a percentage instead.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn each chance into a percentage to one decimal place.

explain.text: As percentages, 3/8 = 37.5%, 5/13 ≈ 38.5% and 7/18 ≈ 38.9%. So the order is 3/8, 38%, 5/13, 7/18. One decimal place is enough to separate them.
